info.name: notification-service
info.description:
`baseUrl` defaults to http://localhost:8084; `token` is a demo JWT accepted by the service's mock auth (see README, Authentication) and `userId` an arbitrary well-formed UUID.

Health Check and Register Device work standalone. List Notifications and Mark Notification as Read do NOT create their own data: the contract has no public "create" endpoint by design (see README, Endpoints) - notifications only exist once something publishes an event on the notification-events Redis channel. Before running those two, publish a test event yourself first (see README, Events Consumed, for the exact redis-cli command), then set `notificationId` to the id it returns from List Notifications.

item.name: List Notifications (manual step required first - see collection description)

request.description: Returns [] until a test event has been published on the notification-events Redis channel for this userId - there is no HTTP endpoint that creates one (by design, see README). Publish one first with the redis-cli command in the README's Events Consumed section, then run this and copy an id from the response into the notificationId variable for the next request.

item.name: Mark Notification as Read (manual step required first - see collection description)

request.description: Set the notificationId variable to a real id from List Notifications first (which itself requires publishing a test event via redis-cli - see README). Will 404 against the default empty notificationId.
